question: On the unchanged 14 l=2 volcano classes, does the floor/crater IC effect survive when prime-abscissa:size=32 is replaced by prime-projected-abscissa:size=32, or was the effect mediated by cofactor-class dead weight?

claims.text: Every completed row recovers and verifies its planted scalar.
The projected-base IC floor/crater effect either persists below the preregistered 0.97 margin or is equivalent within +/-3% with model heterogeneity no larger than the old null p95.
claims.if_supported: Within this 24-bit split-crater panel only, proceed to charged representative-selection arms on the projected baseline.
claims.if_not_supported: Close the representative-selection lead as mediated by raw cofactor dead weight and absorbed by LEAD-19 within this scope.

claims.text: Projection changes relation yield and counted S relative to the raw base on otherwise identical workloads.
claims.if_supported: Report the paired effect as engineering and retain the matched-rho distance.
claims.if_not_supported: Report no transferable LEAD-19 effect on this prime-field panel.

claims.text: No exponent, scaling, generic-ECC, standardized-curve, or security claim is licensed by this 24-bit panel.

hypotheses.statement: After subgroup projection, l=2 volcano floors still have lower IC relation yield and higher end-to-end counted cost than craters by more than a 3% equivalence margin.
hypotheses.mechanism: If the effect is intrinsic to level-dependent coordinate factor-base realization, projection removes dead cofactor classes but leaves a floor/crater contrast; if it was cofactor-class mediation, projection removes it.

predictions.minimum_effect: 90% CI upper endpoint below 0.97 and one-sided permutation p < 0.05

data_seen.measured: binary-curve projected-base transfer, not this prime-field population

provenance.decisive_scope: The projected prime-base rows have never been run; the classes and raw outcomes are already seen.

hypotheses.statement: The cofactor projection increases useful relation yield and lowers end-to-end S versus the raw base on the same prime-field workloads.
hypotheses.mechanism: Multiplication by h maps scanned rational points into the r-order subgroup, eliminating table entries that cannot match a subgroup target while charging the projection work.

predictions.minimum_effect: paired relation-yield ratio 95% CI lower endpoint above 1; any S ordering must hold at native-operation prices 0, 0.1, and 1 GAE

data_seen.measured: 1.29x to 3.36x binary-ladder S lever at cofactors 2 to 6

provenance.decisive_scope: Prime-field cofactor-4/12 volcano classes and the registered projected prime-abscissa implementation.

arms.description: Matched rho.negation on every workload; also the across-level negative control.
Unmodified raw prime-abscissa:size=32 base with the frozen negation-folded MITM oracle; the prior H1 is the positive control.
The sole treatment: prime-projected-abscissa:size=32 with the same oracle and every other workload and budget fixed.
rho.negation repeated under a second arm name for the matched A/A admission control.

positive.not_applicable_reason: No extra positive-control arm is added because it would change the frozen cost population. Instead the unchanged ic-raw baseline is a mandatory in-session detector calibration: it must reproduce the already-confirmed floor deficit (90% CI upper endpoint below 0.97 and p < 0.05), and a miss invalidates every projected null conclusion. The separate synthetic 0.95 floor plant must also be detected by the frozen analysis.

negative.not_applicable_reason: No extra negative-control arm is needed because the matched rho-neg reference already supplies the exact null path on every retained workload; its +/-3% level-equivalence result is a mandatory invalidation gate. The previously measured 14-class l=3 null is retained as an already-seen calibration and cannot decide the projected result.

factors.name: population
factors.value: 14 l=2 v2.1 classes; 3,904 curve-models; 8 targets each
factors.how: Specs slice the committed ordered curves arrays; source spec hashes and slice bounds are in specs/manifest.json.

factors.name: factor_base
factors.how: Both arms run in each cell against the same workload and algorithm seed.

factors.name: volcano_level
factors.how: The original curves.jsonl sidecars fix vertex, model, and level before this protocol.

factors.name: oracle
factors.how: Written explicitly in both IC arms.

factors.name: instrument
factors.value: one release ecbench binary and digest-pinned OCI image per submitted population
factors.how: same_instrument_as binds all arms; request and result must match the frozen source and image.

factors.name: threads
factors.how: The ecbench child environment fixes Rayon and OpenMP to one thread.

factors.name: algorithm_seed
factors.how: ecbench derives a seed per workload and round from each frozen spec's measurement seed and shares it across arms.

factors.name: arm_order
factors.how: Shuffle order is fixed by each spec before data and interleaves arms within every round.

factors.name: class_and_shard
factors.how: All 104 disjoint cells run; cell membership is not a selection variable.

factors.name: host_and_load
factors.how: EKS/ecbench records CPU, kernel, NUMA, SMT, PSI, steal, foreign slices, run queue, interrupts, and L2 blockers per row.

factors.name: uncharged_native_work
factors.how: Every emitted counter is retained and priced at 0, 0.1, and 1 GAE for raw, projected, and rho.

comparisons.threshold: floor/crater 90% CI upper endpoint below 0.97 and p < 0.05

transfer_obligations.obligation: The result transfers only to the committed 24-bit prime-field split-crater depth-3 population.
A projected-base gain is engineering and does not transfer an exponent improvement to generic ECC or ECC2K-130.

seed_derivation.note: Each generated spec retains the source class measurement seed (1001 through 1014); ecbench freezes the per-workload, per-round algorithm seeds in plan.json and shares them across arms.

instance_sampling.rule: Complete census of the committed l=2 v2.1 class exports, preserving all 3,904 curve-models and their eight target_seed-derived planted_shared targets.

blinding.how: Not masked: arm implementations are structurally visible in emitted factor-base counters. The analysis script, margins, direction, and verdicts are frozen before data.

power.note: Fourteen classes, 3,904 models, eight targets and five algorithm-seed rounds greatly exceed v2.1, whose predicted four-class precision was about +/-0.9% for a 6.5% effect. The primary equivalence margin is +/-3%; 10,000 permutations resolve alpha 0.05. Repeated rounds are sampled within curve by the frozen two-stage analysis.

preflight_runtime.measured_on: The complete old l=2 main sessions took 44,873.130 s for 124,928 arm-round executions; the new four-arm, six-round design is 6x, about 74.8 CPU-hours. <=40-model cells predict <=46 minutes at the old mean, below the 3,600 s request cap.

primary.name: end-to-end counted S
primary.definition: All charged factor-base, relation, linear-algebra, and verification group-addition equivalents for one solve, divided by sqrt(r).

primary.name: relations per target tried
primary.definition: relations_found divided by targets_tried over the same end-to-end IC row; no failed row is dropped.
primary.resolution: one relation and one target trial

primary.name: class-stratified floor/crater ratio
primary.definition: Within each class, ratio of the floor to crater aggregate, combined as the equal-weight mean of log ratios.
primary.resolution: recorded f64 from exact integer counters

primary.name: isomorphic-model heterogeneity tau
primary.definition: DerSimonian-Laird relative spread between isomorphic models within class, vertex, and level.
primary.resolution: recorded f64 from exact integer counters

primary.name: S at native-operation prices 0, 0.1, and 1
primary.definition: Recorded S plus each emitted uncharged native-operation count times the common price, divided by sqrt(r).
primary.resolution: 0.1 GAE / sqrt(r) at the middle price

secondary.name: solve wall time
secondary.definition: The ecbench solve interval in a fresh child, reported only for rows that earn L2 and read against the same-session rho A/A interval.

placement.submission: all frozen cells submitted once without waiting for scientific outcomes; the existing 32-vCPU pool queues excess cells

stopping_rules.rule: Fixed design: all 104 manifest cells, each with 4 arms x its frozen workloads x (1 warmup + 5 measured rounds), then stop.
A non-verified row, timeout, algorithm error, or exhausted cell is recorded and is not retried for its result; only a launcher-classified infrastructure failure may use the one allowed retry.
No early success stop and no cell cancellation based on interim counters, cost, yield, level, or arm.

invalidation_rules: Any missing manifest cell or any measured outcome other than verified makes the scientific verdict invalid; all rows remain reported.
A request/spec/source/image/binary identity mismatch makes that cell invalid and forbids silent substitution.
Failure of raw H1 positive control, rho level negative control, rho A/A admission, L2 admission, payload hashes, or replay-all makes the projected null invalid.
Wall time on a row below L2 is descriptive only; counted units remain usable only when the row and its replay verify.
A missing uncharged counter makes the corresponding price-band ordering a lower bound and withholds a rank claim.

decision_rule.text: After every gate passes: verdict mediated_by_raw_cofactor_dead_weight when ic-projected floor/crater 90% CI is contained in [0.97,1.03] and model tau <= 0.047; verdict projected_level_effect_persists when the interval excludes 1 with upper endpoint < 0.97 and one-sided permutation p < 0.05; otherwise inconclusive. Any gate failure is invalid_measurement. The projection transfer is separately supported only when its paired relation-yield interval is above 1 and any S ordering holds at 0, 0.1, and 1 GAE/native-op.
decision_rule.threshold: Primary equivalence [0.97,1.03], persistence upper CI < 0.97 and p < 0.05, model tau gate 0.047
decision_rule.statistic: Equal-class-weight mean log floor/crater ratio with two-stage bootstrap and class-stratified level-label permutation; paired candidate/raw ratios for transfer
decision_rule.interval: 90% bootstrap for the equivalence/level decision; 95% paired bootstrap for candidate/raw and price-band comparisons
decision_rule.effect_size_measure: floor/crater ratio, model tau, projected/raw relation-yield ratio, and projected/raw S ratio across the full price band

graphs: projected and raw floor/crater ratios with 90% intervals
per-level S and relation yield for raw and projected arms
per-class projected effect and isomorphic-model heterogeneity
projected/raw price-band forest at 0, 0.1, and 1 GAE

inadmissible: changing a class, curve-model, target, shard, seed, arm, round count, oracle, factor-base size, direction, margin, or verdict after affected data
dropping or rerunning a cell because its scientific result is inconvenient
combining rows from different source, spec, image, binary, or unverified payload identities
selecting one price from the 0/0.1/1 band or omitting an emitted native counter
quoting wall time from below-L2 rows or using it when the A/A control fails
calling a constant engineering improvement an exponent or generic-ECC advance
publishing a leaderboard or benchmark row before independent replay, independent recompute, matched rho band, and VALIDATION.json pass

literature.claim: Cofactor projection removes dead factor-base classes on the binary ladder and specifies the charged mechanism and validation debt.
The raw-base 14-class l=2 floor deficit, controls, population, original runtime, and exact class exports reused here.
The projected-base rerun is the cheap discriminator; it fixes the 3% equivalence rule, 0.047 model null, and scope limits.
Counted S, paired comparisons, L2/A/A admission, pricing band, replay, and publication validation rules.

literature.ref: Tate isogeny theorem; Faugere-Gaudry-Huot-Renault, Journal of Cryptology 27 (2014), as provenance-recorded in the E4 desk card
literature.claim: Isogenous curves share group order; extension-field symmetry results do not supply this prime-field projected-base effect.
